title: EmbeddingReplayBuffer replay is fundamentally broken: task_ids used as class keys, label_offset=0 collides tasks, wrong head/labels
description: populate() keys the store by raw class label c=int(lbl.item())+label_offset (435) with label_offset=0 at BOTH call sites (1011, 1079), so SHD classes 0-9 OVERWRITE N-MNIST classes 0-9 in the shared _store dict (self._store[c]=... at 443). sample(task_ids) then treats task_ids as store KEYS, not task ids: available=[c for c in task_ids if c in self._store] (449). Call sites pass replay_task_ids=[1] (1050) and [1,2] (1102), so replay draws only class-index 1 (and 2) embeddings from whatever task last wrote those keys, never a task's worth of samples and never N-MNIST (it was overwritten). The sampled labels are the class indices (457) and are fed to forward_from_embeddings(embs, task_name) through the CURRENT task's head (611-615), so replay optimizes the wrong head against wrong labels. _task_labels[c]=task_id (444) records the true task but sample() never consults it. Net effect: 'embedding replay' rehearses one-to-two wrong-task embeddings through the current head, so it cannot prevent forgetting of prior tasks. This is the hub imported by 19 files, so the defect propagates everywhere.
evidence: key c=int(lbl.item())+label_offset (435); self._store[c]=torch.stack(samples) (443); self._task_labels[c]=task_id (444, unused by sample); available=[c for c in task_ids if c in self._store] (449); label_offset=0 (1011,1079); replay_task_ids=[1] (1050), [1,2] (1102); forward_from_embeddings(replay_embs, task_name) (612-614). The CORRECT pattern is present in the same file: RawInputReplayBuffer.sample filters by task_names (498-508).
fix: Key the buffer per task so tasks cannot collide (offset labels by task, or nest by task_id); in sample() select stored classes via _task_labels==requested task_id (mirror RawInputReplayBuffer.sample, 498); replay each sample through its OWN task head with its own labels, not the current task_name. Same defect and the same fix apply to the orphan clone code/m7_trimodal_run.py.

title: Default forward path silently routes features through proj_shared/proj_private (512->128+384->512), diverging from the documented architecture and from the orphan copy
description: forward() (401-407) always calls forward_with_shared() (372-399), which always calls _split_shared_private() (394): shared=proj_shared(features) (364), private=proj_private(features) (368), full=cat([shared,private]) (369). The memory stack then consumes full, not the raw backbone features (gate=adaptive_gate(full) 395, hop=hopfield(full) 396, hgrn=hgrn(full) 397). proj_shared and proj_private are independent trainable nn.Linear layers, so full = W*features + b is an EXTRA learned 512->512 reparametrisation inserted before Hopfield/HGRN/gate. This projection is documented (forward_with_shared docstring, 372-376) as used only 'during cross-modal alignment training', yet it is active on every forward pass even with align_cross_modal=False (the default, 1321). The orphan copy code/m7_trimodal_run.py feeds RAW features to the same modules (m7_trimodal_run.py:338-340), and CLAUDE.md documents the pipeline as backbone->Hopfield||HGRN->gate with no shared/private split. So the shared hub runs a different, higher-capacity model than both the docs and the nominal reproducibility entry point, changing numerics.
evidence: self.proj_shared=nn.Linear(cfg.shared_dim, cfg.align_shared_dim) built unconditionally (337); _split_shared_private returns full=cat([shared,private]) (369); forward_with_shared uses gate/hop/hgrn on full (395-398); forward delegates to forward_with_shared (406). Contrast orphan m7_trimodal_run.py:338-340 which uses raw features.
fix: Only apply the shared/private projection when cfg.align_cross_modal (or an explicit flag) is set; otherwise feed raw backbone features to gate/hopfield/hgrn so the default model matches the documented architecture and the orphan. If the projection is intended to be permanent, document it in CLAUDE.md/EXPERIMENTAL_MANIFEST and reconcile the orphan copy. Any change here moves numbers: call it out with before/after.

title: Replay path (forward_from_embeddings) bypasses _split_shared_private, so replayed embeddings hit a different subgraph than live inputs
description: Live inputs are transformed by _split_shared_private into full before gate/hopfield/hgrn (394-398). But forward_from_embeddings(embs, task_name) (409-414) applies adaptive_gate/hopfield/hgrn DIRECTLY to the stored embeddings, skipping proj_shared/proj_private entirely. The stored embeddings are raw backbone features (populate calls model._get_features, 433, which returns backbone output). So replay trains gate/Hopfield/HGRN/heads on raw-feature distribution while inference uses the projected full distribution — a train/inference mismatch that corrupts the replay gradient even if PROV-001 were fixed. This inconsistency is PROVENANCE-SPECIFIC: in the orphan both live and replay paths use raw features (m7_trimodal_run.py:338-340 vs 344-349), so they are consistent there. The bug was introduced by the proj insertion in PROV-002.
evidence: forward_from_embeddings: gate=adaptive_gate(embs), hop=hopfield(embs) on raw embs (410-411); live path uses full via _split_shared_private (394-398); populate stores model._get_features(...) raw features (433, 359-360).
fix: Route replayed embeddings through the same _split_shared_private transform used for live inputs before gate/hopfield/hgrn, OR store the post-projection full representation in the buffer. Keep replay and inference on the identical subgraph.

title: Best-validation weights are never restored: reported best_val, saved checkpoint, and test_acc all use the final (post-early-stopping) epoch
description: train_task tracks best_val as a scalar (662-663) but never snapshots the weights at that epoch. Early stopping breaks after patience epochs of no improvement (665-669), leaving the model in a degraded post-peak state. test_acc is then computed on that final state (671) and the checkpoint saved by run_one_seed is model.state_dict() at end of training (1003, 1054, 1106) — i.e. final-epoch, not best. So the returned best_val does not correspond to the weights that produce test_acc or to the weights saved and reloaded on the next task. Reporting best_val alongside a test number from different weights is misleading. Note the orphan clone at least saves a best_*.pt (m7_trimodal_run.py:488-495) but also never reloads it before test — provenance dropped even that save.
evidence: best_val updated but no best-state kept (662-664); early stop break (667-669); test_acc=self.evaluate(test_loader,...) after loop on final weights (671); torch.save(model.state_dict()) final-epoch (1003,1054,1106).
fix: Snapshot state_dict when val improves (copy.deepcopy) and reload it before computing test_acc and before saving the checkpoint, so best_val, the test metric, and the persisted weights are mutually consistent. Do the same in the orphan.

title: forgetting_T1_T3 uses the after-T2 accuracy as its baseline, inconsistent with the other two forgetting metrics (mislabeled)
description: forgetting_T1_T2 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t2 (1133) and forgetting_T2_T3 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_after_t3 (1135) both measure drop from a task's OWN post-training accuracy (cumulative forgetting). But forgetting_T1_T3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3 (1134) measures the INCREMENTAL drop between the after-T2 and after-T3 stages, not cumulative T1 forgetting after T3. A reader interpreting 'forgetting_T1_T3' as T1 forgetting measured after T3 would expect acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3. The three metrics therefore do not share one definition, and any total-forgetting summary built from them is wrong. Identical bug in the orphan (m7_trimodal_run.py:613-615). Forgetting is a RULE-5-sensitive claim.
evidence: forgetting_t1_t2 = acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t2 (1133); forgetting_t1_t3 = acc_t1_after_t2 - acc_t1_after_t3 (1134); forgetting_t2_t3 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_after_t3 (1135). acc_t1_after set at 1007, acc_t1_after_t2 at 1061, acc_t1_after_t3 at 1113.
fix: Decide one definition. For cumulative forgetting after T3 use acc_t1_after - acc_t1_after_t3; if the incremental T2->T3 drop is genuinely wanted, rename it (e.g. forgetting_T1_incremental_T3). Apply the same rename/fix to the orphan.

title: Results CSV is appended without dedup and aggregated without dedup; schema also diverges from the orphan and from the canonical loader
description: save_seed_result appends each seed's row to cl_trimodal_results.csv via read+concat+write (853-856) with NO dedup, so reruns accumulate duplicate rows. aggregate_results reads that master (883), filters only df['T1_after_T1'].notna() (885), and computes mean/std/CI/Wilcoxon over the raw rows (888-936) — duplicates inflate n and corrupt std/CI exactly as warned in the repo's own load_results.py. Separately, the schema DIVERGES: this file writes summary rows with NO 'step' column and columns T2_fwt/T3_fwt (1154-1155, plus T2_zero_shot/T3_zero_shot/T2_learning_gain/etc.), whereas the orphan writes incremental rows WITH a 'step' column plus a single 'fwt' column (m7_trimodal_run.py:630, 687-697). The documented pandas ritual df[df['step'].isna()] (python-numerics rule 3) KeyErrors on this file's CSV because there is no 'step' column, and the canonical loader looks for a 'fwt' column (load_results.py:206) this file never writes. Because both hubs write the SAME filename ./ICONS_M7/results/cl_trimodal_results.csv, mixing runs yields inconsistent columns and the notna filter would even keep the orphan's step-rows (their T1_after_T1 is populated).
evidence: append without dedup (853-856); aggregate filters notna only, no drop_duplicates (885-905); ci/std over raw rows (894-896); T2_fwt/T3_fwt (1154-1155); orphan writes 'step' rows and 'fwt' (m7_trimodal_run.py:687-697, 630); canonical loader expects step + fwt (load_results.py:82,206).
fix: Deduplicate to one row per (seed, condition) before aggregating (reuse .claude/skills/analyze-cl-results/scripts/load_results.py). Standardise a single CSV schema across both hubs (or write distinct filenames) and align column names (fwt vs T2_fwt/T3_fwt, step column) with the canonical loader.

title: Two divergent copies of the model+trainer share class/function names and output filenames but differ in model math, metrics, CSV schema, freezing, and import-safety
description: m7_trimodal_run_provenance.py (the shared hub, referenced by 19 files) and code/m7_trimodal_run.py (the orphan, imported by nobody) define the SAME public names — M7_ContinualAdaptiveModel, ContinualLearner, EmbeddingReplayBuffer, SNN_Backbone, run_one_seed, TASKS, collate fns — yet have DIVERGED substantially: (1) provenance inserts a proj_shared/proj_private reparametrisation into the forward path, the orphan does not (PROV-002); (2) provenance freezes completed backbones/heads via _freeze_completed_tasks (550-568), the orphan freezes nothing so it trains all params every task; (3) provenance defines 'fwt' as zero_shot - random_init (1066) while the orphan defines 'fwt' as after - zero_shot (m7_trimodal_run.py:616) — a different, mislabeled quantity (PROV-008); (4) different CSV schema and filename collision (PROV-006); (5) provenance is import-safe with a __main__ guard, the orphan runs a 4-5h job at import. Both write ./ICONS_M7/results/cl_trimodal_results.csv and identical checkpoint names (final_{task}_{task}_seed{seed}_{condition}.pt), so their artifacts are mutually confusable while their numerics differ. Edits to one will not propagate to the other.
evidence: Shared names across both files; _freeze_completed_tasks present only in provenance (550-568); fwt formulas differ (1066 vs m7_trimodal_run.py:616); identical checkpoint naming (1) prov 992/1041/1093 (2) orphan 536/562/589; __main__ guard prov 1378 vs orphan top-level run 707-711.
fix: Collapse to a single source of truth: keep the provenance hub, delete or clearly quarantine the orphan (it is imported by nobody), or extract the shared model/trainer into one module both import. At minimum stop them writing identical filenames.

title: 'fwt' means different things in the two hubs; the orphan's formula is learning-gain mislabeled as forward transfer, and only that mislabel can produce a large positive FWT
description: This file computes fwt_t2 = acc_t2_zero_shot - random_init_baselines[task2] (1066): zero-shot accuracy on T2 (with an untrained T2 head, measured after T1) minus a fresh-random-init baseline. Because the T2 head is randomly initialised in BOTH terms, both are near chance and this FWT is ~0 by construction (print_task_sanity even warns if zero_shot deviates >5pp from chance, 840-841). That is the honest forward-transfer measure. The orphan clone instead computes fwt = acc_t2_after_t2 - acc_t2_zero_shot (m7_trimodal_run.py:616), which is the TRAINING gain on T2, not transfer, yet is stored under the name 'fwt'. Any large positive 'FWT' figure (the docs quote ~75 pp, unsourced per RULE 1) can only arise from the orphan's mislabeled learning-gain formula, not from a real forward-transfer computation. This directly bears on contested-fact #4 (the two cross-modal-transfer narratives).
evidence: prov: fwt_t2 = acc_t2_zero_shot - random_init_baselines[task2] (1066); learning_gain_t2 = acc_t2_after - acc_t2_zero_shot computed separately (1065); orphan: fwt = acc_t2_after_t2 - acc_t2_zero_shot (m7_trimodal_run.py:616). Sanity warns if zero_shot far from chance (840).
fix: Rename the orphan's 'fwt' to 'learning_gain' (it is not forward transfer). Keep this file's FWT definition, and when any FWT number is reported, state which formula produced it and report it with its near-chance baseline. Do not repeat the ~75 pp FWT claim without a CSV.

title: '95% CI' uses the normal quantile 1.96 for tiny seed counts and returns a zero-width CI at n=1
description: aggregate_results computes ci95 = 1.96 * std / sqrt(n) if n>1 else 0.0 (896). With the small seed counts this project uses (3, or the 5 in the default seeds list), the correct multiplier is the Student-t quantile (t.975 = 4.30 at n=3, 2.78 at n=5), not 1.96, so the interval is materially too narrow and mislabeled as a 95% CI. When n==1 the code emits ci95=0.0, so ci95_lower==ci95_upper==mean (903-904) — a fabricated zero-uncertainty interval rather than an undefined one. std uses ddof=1 (894), which is NaN at n=1.
evidence: ci95 = 1.96 * std / np.sqrt(n) if n > 1 else 0.0 (896); ci95_lower/upper = mean -/+ ci95 (903-904); std = sub.std(ddof=1) (894).
fix: Use scipy.stats.t.ppf(0.975, df=n-1) for the multiplier (scipy is already imported, 23), and emit NaN (not 0) for n<2. Label it a t-based CI.

title: Wilcoxon signed-rank on 3-5 paired seeds is underpowered and cannot reach significance; also a dead 'seeds' variable
description: aggregate_results runs stats.wilcoxon(diff) on per-seed paired differences (920) where the number of pairs equals the seed count (3, or up to 5). At n=3 the smallest achievable two-sided p is ~0.25, so no result can be significant and any reported p-value is misleading; even n=5 is far below the sample size where Wilcoxon is meaningful. The guard only checks that at least one difference is nonzero (919), not that n is adequate. Separately, seeds = df['seed'].unique() (911) is assigned and never used.
evidence: stat, pval = stats.wilcoxon(diff) (920) with len(paired) potentially 3-5 (916); seeds = df['seed'].unique() unused (911).
fix: Do not report a Wilcoxon p-value at these sample sizes; report the paired mean difference and its spread, or gather many more seeds before any significance test. Remove the unused seeds variable.

title: random_init_baseline reseeds the global torch RNG and leaves it altered before training starts, coupling training determinism to the baseline procedure
description: run_one_seed sets torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed) and np.random.seed(cfg.seed) (964-965) and constructs the real model at 971 (so model init is deterministic). It then calls random_init_baseline for each task (982-984), which internally does torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed + 1000 + s) three times per task (812) and builds throwaway models. After the loop the global torch RNG is left at the last baseline seed's consumed state, NOT at manual_seed(cfg.seed). Training then begins (997) drawing DataLoader shuffling and any stochastic ops from that leftover state. Consequently the training RNG stream depends on how many baseline seeds/tasks were run: changing n_seeds (currently 3, hardcoded at 983) or task_order silently changes training results, so the run is not numerically inert to a change that ought to be inert. The reported cfg.seed also does not cleanly map to the training RNG state.
evidence: torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed) (964); model built (971); random_init_baseline(...) loop (982-984) calls torch.manual_seed(cfg.seed + 1000 + s) (812) and builds models (813); training starts at 997 with no reseed.
fix: Isolate baseline RNG (use a local torch.Generator, or save/restore torch.get_rng_state() around random_init_baseline), then reseed to cfg.seed immediately before training so the training stream is a deterministic function of cfg.seed alone.

title: Default seeds list is five seeds, deviating from the documented 3-seed policy [42,123,456] and from the orphan
description: ExperimentConfig.seeds defaults to [42, 123, 456, 789, 101112] (63) and main() sets the same (1320), so the default run is 5 seeds x 2 conditions = 10 runs. The documented policy (CLAUDE.md, python-numerics rule 4, load_results.py DOCUMENTED_SEEDS) is [42, 123, 456], and the orphan uses SEEDS=[42,123,456] (m7_trimodal_run.py:516). More seeds is not itself wrong, but the undocumented deviation means the hub and the orphan produce different-n results, the canonical loader's seed-policy gate is calibrated to three seeds, and any 'n-seed' label must be checked against which pipeline ran.
evidence: seeds default [42,123,456,789,101112] (63); main base_cfg seeds=[42,123,456,789,101112] (1320); orphan SEEDS=[42,123,456] (m7_trimodal_run.py:516); DOCUMENTED_SEEDS={42,123,456} (load_results.py:49).
fix: Align the default seed list with the documented policy, or document and justify the 5-seed choice in CLAUDE.md/EXPERIMENTAL_MANIFEST and update the canonical loader's expected-seeds gate accordingly.

title: The 'per-seed' CSV actually stores the entire accumulated master table, not that seed's row
description: save_seed_result reassigns df to the full master (existing rows + new row) at 855, writes the master (856), then writes df again to cl_results_seed{seed}_{condition}.csv (859-860). Because df is the concatenated master, the file labelled per-seed contains EVERY seed/condition accumulated so far, not one seed. The comment 'Also save per-seed CSV for clean aggregation' (858) is therefore false, and downstream code expecting one row per file gets a growing full history mislabeled by whichever seed happened to be written last.
evidence: df = pd.concat([existing, df], ignore_index=True) (855); df.to_csv(csv_path) master (856); seed_csv = ... (859); df.to_csv(seed_csv) writes the SAME master df (860).
fix: Write only the current seed's row to the per-seed file: build a fresh single-row frame (e.g. pd.DataFrame([result])) for seed_csv instead of reusing the concatenated df.

title: SupCon losses count the anchor itself as a positive (diagonal not masked); the CrossModal comment claiming self contributes zero is wrong
description: SupervisedContrastiveLoss.forward builds mask = eq(labels_i, labels_j) which is True on the diagonal (159), and mean_log_prob = (mask*log_prob).sum(1)/(mask.sum(1)+eps) (164), so each anchor's own similarity is counted in both numerator and denominator of the positive average. Standard SupCon (Khosla et al. 2020) excludes the anchor from its positive set P(i); including it biases the loss toward the trivially-satisfied self term and dilutes the true-positive gradient. This loss is ACTIVE in the default run (scl_weight=0.1, use_scl=True, 608-609). CrossModalSupConLoss repeats the same self-as-positive construction (192,198,202) and its comment (201) asserts 'self gives 0 contribution since mask*log_prob on diagonal is log(1)=0' — that is incorrect: the diagonal log_prob is log-softmax of the self position (<=0), not 0. The CrossModal loss only runs under align_cross_modal (default off), but the misleading comment and the shared bug pattern should be fixed.
evidence: SCL: mask includes diagonal (159); mean over positives incl. self (164); used in train_task (585,609). XMSCL: pos_mask=mask (198), denom incl. self (200), wrong comment (201).
fix: Mask the diagonal out of the positive set (set self-similarity to -inf before softmax and zero it in pos_mask/pos-count) to match Khosla SupCon; correct or delete the false comment at 201. Numerics-affecting: flag before/after if applied.

title: Many ExperimentConfig fields are never consumed; some advertise values the run silently ignores (max_epochs, patience, dropout)
description: Grep confirms zero cfg.-qualified reads for optimizer (37), max_epochs (41), patience (42), dropout (45), hidden_dim (46), num_gru_layers (50), num_workers (51), pin_memory (53), time_steps (52); and align_joint_training (66), align_mixed_batches (67), nmnist_train_per_class (74) are referenced nowhere. Several are actively misleading: max_epochs=50 and patience=12 are ignored because train_task is called with num_epochs=15, patience=5 hardcoded (999,1048,1100); dropout=0.2 is advertised but the model contains no dropout layer; num_workers is hardcoded to 0 in every DataLoader; time_steps=25 is hardcoded in the collate fns (see PROV-018); optimizer='AdamW' is hardcoded (580). A reader trusting the config for reproducibility gets the wrong epoch/patience/dropout.
evidence: cfg.max_epochs/patience/dropout/hidden_dim/num_gru_layers/num_workers/pin_memory/time_steps/optimizer: 0 cfg-qualified references (grep); train_task called num_epochs=15 patience=5 (999,1048,1100); AdamW hardcoded (580); num_workers=0 literal (e.g. 1187-1193).
fix: Either wire these fields into the code (pass cfg.max_epochs/cfg.patience/cfg.num_workers/cfg.time_steps/cfg.optimizer through, add the dropout layer) or delete them from ExperimentConfig so the config cannot misrepresent the run.

title: build_data_loaders unconditionally imports and builds the paired cross-modal loader from the legacy root package, coupling the hub to Dataloaders/ even when alignment is off
description: build_data_loaders does 'from Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader import get_paired_digit_loaders' (1251) and then constructs paired_loader (1262-1271) UNCONDITIONALLY, even though the paired loader is only consumed when cfg.align_cross_modal is True (1017). The hub has no sys.path insertion, so this import requires each of the 19 importing callers to have already put the repo root on sys.path; if not, build_data_loaders raises ModuleNotFoundError. It also does real work (materialising paired samples) in the common case where it is never used. This couples the shared hub to the legacy bi-modal package that CLAUDE.md marks as separate from M7.
evidence: from Dataloaders.paired_digit_loader import get_paired_digit_loaders (1251); paired_loader built unconditionally (1262-1271); only used under cfg.align_cross_modal (1017); no sys.path insert in this file (grep).
fix: Build the paired loader only when cfg.align_cross_modal, and move/guard the import behind that flag. If cross-modal alignment is a first-class hub feature, vendor the needed loader into code/ so the hub does not depend on the legacy root package or on caller sys.path setup.

title: Entire SHD train and test sets are densified into Python lists in memory before any training
description: build_data_loaders materialises every SHD sample into a dense (100,1,1,700) float tensor via list comprehensions over the full datasets (1212-1213) before constructing loaders. Each dense sample is 100*700=70000 floats (~0.27 MB); across the full SHD train+test this is on the order of gigabytes held resident, which is wasteful on MPS/limited-RAM machines and duplicates the same eager pattern as the orphan (m7_trimodal_run.py:149-150). It also runs at build time for every invocation regardless of whether SHD is the current task.
evidence: shd_train_data = [_events_to_dense(e,l) for e,l in tqdm(shd_train,...)] (1212); shd_test_data likewise (1213); dense zeros(100,700) per sample (1201-1202).
fix: Wrap SHD in a lazy Dataset that densifies per-item in __getitem__ (or a DiskCachedDataset like N-MNIST) instead of building full in-memory lists, so memory scales with batch size, not dataset size.

title: Timestep count is inconsistent: cfg.time_steps=25 is dead, visual/DVS are cropped to 25 frames, but SHD runs at 100 timesteps
description: cfg.time_steps=25 (52) is never read (PROV-015). The visual and DVS collate fns hard-crop/pad to 25 frames (113-116, 133-140), but SHD is densified to 100 time bins (_events_to_dense time_bins=100, 1201) and shd_collate_fn does no crop/pad (121-123), so SHD tensors reach the model with T=100. Since every backbone loops over T=x.size(1) (275, 353), N-MNIST/DVS run 25 steps while SHD runs 100 — a 4x difference in temporal depth. This makes cfg.time_steps=25 doubly misleading and complicates the mandatory 'accuracy travels with timestep count' reporting, because the per-task timestep cost is not the single documented value.
evidence: shd_collate_fn stacks without crop (121-123); _events_to_dense time_bins=100 (1201); nmnist/dvs cropped to 25 (113-116,133-140); model loops T=x.size(1) (275,353); cfg.time_steps unread (grep).
fix: Make the timestep count explicit and consistent: either drive all collate/densify paths from cfg.time_steps, or document per-modality timestep counts and report accuracy alongside the actual per-task T (25 visual / 100 audio). Remove or wire cfg.time_steps.

title: Unused imports: os, sys, time, copy, and typing Optional/Tuple/Dict
description: Grep over the whole file (excluding import lines) finds no use of os (7), sys (8), time (9), or the copy module (10) — the only 'copy' token is the pandas .copy() method at 885. From typing (14), Optional and Tuple and Dict are never used (List is). These are harmless but are dead code in the shared hub.
evidence: os/sys/time/copy: 0 uses outside imports (grep); typing Optional/Tuple/Dict: 0 uses; List used at 36,62-63,873.
fix: Remove the unused imports (os, sys, time, copy, Optional, Tuple, Dict). Note copy would become NEEDED if PROV-004 is fixed with copy.deepcopy.

title: safe_empty_cache is defined but never called
description: safe_empty_cache (89-91) empties the CUDA cache but is not called anywhere in this file (grep). It is dead code carried over from the orphan (m7_trimodal_run.py:20-22, also unused there).
evidence: def safe_empty_cache at 89; no call sites in file.
fix: Remove it, or call it at appropriate points (e.g. between tasks) if cache pressure is a real concern; currently it is inert.

title: EmbeddingReplayBuffer default device picks mps/cpu only, ignoring CUDA
description: When device is None the buffer defaults to mps if available else cpu (419-420), never cuda. run_one_seed passes an explicit device (975) so the default is not hit there, but any of the 19 importers that construct EmbeddingReplayBuffer without a device on a CUDA host would place replay embeddings on CPU while the model is on CUDA, causing a device-mismatch error in forward_from_embeddings.
evidence: device = torch.device('mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else 'cpu') (420); explicit device passed at 975.
fix: Mirror get_device precedence (mps -> cuda -> cpu) in the buffer default, or make device a required argument.

title: Output/data paths are CWD-relative ('./ICONS_M7'), so a hub used by 19 callers writes wherever each caller's CWD happens to be
description: main() sets base_dir=Path('./ICONS_M7') (1285) and build_data_loaders uses Path('./ICONS_M7/datasets') (1169); both are relative to the current working directory, resolving as documented only when CWD is code/ (CLAUDE.md, python-numerics rule 6). Because this module is imported by 19 files that may run from different directories, results, checkpoints, and datasets can silently land in, or be read from, the wrong place — including the checkpoint-skip trap loading a stale final_*.pt from an unexpected directory.
evidence: base_dir = Path('./ICONS_M7') (1285); data_dir = Path('./ICONS_M7/datasets') (1169); checkpoints under results_dir (1287).
fix: Anchor paths to a stable base (e.g. Path(__file__).resolve().parent or an explicit argument/env var) rather than CWD, or require callers to pass an absolute results/ckpt dir (run_one_seed already accepts results_dir/ckpt_dir — main and build_data_loaders should too).

title: N-MNIST collate silently crops each sample to the first 25 time-windows, discarding most of the temporal window
description: nmnist_collate_fn truncates any sample with more than 25 frames to e[:25] (113-114). With the N-MNIST ToFrame transform (time_window=1000 over ~300 ms recordings) samples contain far more than 25 windows, so only the first ~25 ms of temporal information is used and the rest is dropped without any log. DVS collate does the same (133-135). This is a modeling choice inherited from the orphan, but it materially affects the temporal-cost interpretation and should be surfaced when reporting accuracy with its timestep count.
fix: Document the 25-frame crop (and its effect on effective temporal coverage) where the timestep count is reported; if fuller temporal coverage is intended, subsample or bin across the whole window instead of taking the head.

title: _events_to_dense divides by max_time which can be zero, producing NaN time indices
description: In _events_to_dense, time_indices = (events['t'] / max_time * (time_bins-1)).astype(int) (1205) where max_time = events['t'].max() (1204). If all events share t=0 (or a single event at t=0), max_time is 0 and the division yields inf/NaN, and astype(int) on NaN is undefined behaviour. The len(events)>0 guard (1203) does not cover the all-zero-timestamp case, and the inner 'if len(events)>0 else 1' (1204) is redundant since it is already inside the len>0 block.
evidence: max_time = events['t'].max() if len(events) > 0 else 1 (1204); time_indices = (events['t'] / max_time * (time_bins - 1)).astype(int) (1205).
fix: Guard with max_time = max(events['t'].max(), 1) (or skip the sample) so the divisor is never zero; drop the redundant inner conditional.

title: Redundant duplicate DataLoader instances constructed over the same split
description: For each modality build_data_loaders builds a 'train'/'val'/'test' loader AND a separate 'train_val_test' tuple of loaders over the SAME underlying splits (e.g. N-MNIST 1186-1194). The training path uses train_val_test (997-998) while buffer.populate uses the separate 'train' loader (1011). This doubles loader construction and, because both train loaders have shuffle=True with no fixed generator, they iterate in different orders; it is redundant and mildly confusing rather than incorrect.
evidence: nmnist_loaders 'train' (1187) and 'train_val_test'[0] (1191) both wrap train_split; used at 1011 vs 997-998.
fix: Construct each loader once and reference it in both places, or drop the train_val_test tuple in favour of named keys.

title: Positive: the provenance hub is import-safe (has a __main__ guard and lazy data loading), unlike the orphan
description: Unlike code/m7_trimodal_run.py (which loads datasets and runs the full 4-5h experiment at module import time with no guard), this file has if __name__=='__main__': main() (1378-1379), and all dataset loading/experiment work is inside build_data_loaders/main() called only from that guard. The only top-level side effects are cheap: spike_grad = surrogate.atan() (148) and the TASKS dict (955-959). This matters precisely because the module is imported by 19 files — importing it does NOT trigger the long run. No action needed; recorded so downstream tooling does not treat it like the orphan.
evidence: __main__ guard (1378); data loading inside build_data_loaders (1168) called from main (1339); top-level only spike_grad (148) and TASKS (955).
fix: None required. Preserve the guard and the lazy-loading structure in any refactor.

title: Shared hub contains the SpiNNaker-non-portable ops (LayerNorm, Softmax gate, HGRN multiplicative reset r*h_prev)
description: The model defined here is what the SpiNNaker port must map. It uses nn.LayerNorm inside Hopfield (228) and HGRN (243-245) and in each head (332); a Softmax gate (327); and the HGRN multiplicative reset r * h_prev (254). Per .claude/rules/spinnaker.md and CLAUDE.md, LayerNorm and Softmax are not native to sPyNNaker and the multiplicative reset r*h_prev is flagged as not expressible (risk R3, threatening the novelty claim). This is not a code defect; it is recorded so the port work references the actual hub source rather than the orphan.
evidence: LayerNorm in Hopfield (228), HGRN (243-245), heads (332); Softmax gate (327); h_tilde uses torch.cat([x, r * h_prev]) (254).
fix: No code change here. Use these exact lines as the reference when assessing SpiNNaker expressibility; do not assert portability without a board run (mapping != inference != hardware).
